title: Ohlone - Wikipedia
text: The Ohlone, formerly known as Costanoans, are a Native American people of the Northern California coast. The Ohlone are believed to have displaced an earlier population of Hokan-speaking residents of the area.

title: Ohlone, Northern | Ethnologue Free
text: Northern Ohlone is a dormant language of the United States. It belongs to the Miwok-Costanoan language family.

title: Costanoan Language and the Ohlone Indian Tribes (Karkin, Cholon...)
text: Costanoan/Ohlone Indian Language. The Costanoan languages are considered by most linguists to be part of the Penutian family of languages, most closely related to Miwok. There were once several distinct Costanoan languages, including Mutsun, Rumsen, Karkin, and Cholon.

title: Utian (Miwok-Costanoan) Languages - Sorosoro Sorosoro
text: The speakers of Utian languages are members of the Miwok and Ohlone “First Nations” of North America who already inhabited the region long before Europeans arrived and before the creation of the United States. Total number of speakers (estimated): 15 according to UNESCO.

title: Ohlone: The First Alamedans, “Were Not a ‘Branch of Miwok Indians'”...
text: Here, Merlin refers to Ohlone People (known then, at least, as the Lisyan, Costanoan, and Verona) as a “branch of the Miwok tribe”. The citation for this claim refers to the unpublished, personal correspondence of Robert F. Heizer.

title: Ohlone Facts for Kids
text: Ohlone Tribes & Villages. The Ohlone people, also known as Costanoans, are Native American groups from the coast of Northern California. The name "Costanoan" comes from a Spanish word meaning 'coast dweller'.

title: Northern Ohlone
text: The Ohlone people practiced the Kuksu religion. Prior to the Gold Rush, the northern California region was one of the most densely populated regions north of Mexico.

title: Ohlone-Miwok-Yokuts Mythology - Myths and Legends
text: The Ohlone-Miwok-Yokuts mythology brings together the following Native American peoples: Ohlone, Costanoan, Miwok, Yokut, Mariposan.

title: Ohlone/Costanoan Ethnohistory
text: Northern Ohlone/Costanoan (Mission San Jose) ritual was documented by J. P. Harrington, who learned that the Hiwey, Lole, and Kuksu dances, associated with the cult to the north, were practiced at Mission San Jose.

title: Ohlone - Academic Kids
text: The Ohlone, formerly Costanoan, are an ethnic group whose members lived in what is now the San Francisco Bay Area and Monterey Bay areas of California until after the European discovery and settling of this area.
